papers.title: Associations Between Childhood Sadness and Romantic Relationship Satisfaction in Emerging Adulthood: A Mixed-Methods Exploration Considering Wellbeing and Emotional Dysregulation.
papers.abstract: There has been extensive research on childhood adverse experiences and their impact on interpersonal relationships. However, most studies have focused on trauma or abuse, and on peer or familial relationships; research examining childhood sadness in relation to romantic relationship satisfaction (RRS) in emerging adulthood remains limited. This study, using a mixed methods approach, examines whether childhood sadness is associated with RRS, considering adult wellbeing and emotional dysregulation. In the quantitative component, 217 participants (39 men, 18%; 178 women, 82%; Mage = 21.13, SD = 2.09) were recruited via an online survey using convenience sampling and completed measures of childhood sadness, emotional dysregulation, adult wellbeing, and RRS. Results showed that higher childhood sadness was associated with lower RRS through adult wellbeing. Emotional dysregulation did not independently account for this association; however, exploratory analyses suggested an ordered pattern in which childhood sadness was associated with emotional dysregulation, which was in turn associated with adult wellbeing, and subsequently RRS. In the qualitative component, six participants (2 males, 4 females; Mage = 22.5 years) were recruited using a combination of opportunistic and purposive sampling and completed semi-structured interviews exploring the perceived impact of childhood sadness. Thematic analysis identified four key themes: understanding childhood sadness, emotional dysregulation as a barrier, adult emotional consequences, and romantic relationship challenges. Together, these findings advance understanding of how childhood sadness, adult wellbeing, and emotional dysregulation are associated with RRS, and highlight the potential value of early interventions supporting emotional development and later wellbeing and relationship satisfaction. Directions for future research are also discussed.

papers.title: (Un)tidying the Account: The Emotional Cost of Hearing Untold Stories.
papers.abstract: In qualitative research, the researcher can be considered the research instrument, in which our positionality influences our interactions with participants and our interpretations of the data. Yet, the effect of this process on the researcher is less emphasized. In this essay, I describe the experience of writing my master's thesis about sexual assault survivors' privacy management in romantic relationships, asking how we manage these embodied experiences (and our disclosures of such) as scholars.

papers.title: A Novel Gamified Approach to Measuring Dating Violence Attitudes: The Role of Relationship Self-Efficacy Among University Students.
papers.abstract: This cross-sectional study examined dating violence attitudes and relationship self-efficacy among 381 university students, using a novel gamified platform-a field first-to boost engagement and reduce social desirability bias. Participants rejected violence-tolerant attitudes (DAVS M = 1.91), with sexual violence rated most acceptable. Male students scored higher than females on DAVS total (p < .001) and all five subscales (p < .05). Independent predictors included male gender (β = .237), younger age (β = -.120), relationship duration of 1-3 years (β = .123), and lower relationship self-efficacy (β = -.334). Assessments took 10-12 min; whether gamification improves engagement or reduces bias warrants comparative testing.

papers.title: High diversity and novel host associations of bat haemosporidian parasites in Cambodia: insights from a nationwide bat survey and multilocus analyses.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Haemosporidian ("malaria") parasites are a diverse group of vector-borne apicomplexan parasites that infect a wide range of vertebrate hosts, including humans. Bats harbour a remarkable diversity of haemosporidians and are considered important hosts in the evolution of mammalian haemosporidian lineages, yet parasite diversity, host associations, and evolutionary relationships remain poorly understood, particularly in biodiversity-rich Southeast Asia. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide molecular survey of 1180 bats representing 34 species across Cambodia and combined extensive sampling with multilocus phylogenetic and ecological analyses to investigate haemosporidian diversity, host associations, evolutionary relationships, and ecological correlates of infection. RESULTS: Haemosporidian infections were detected in 12.9% of the sampled bats and comprised diverse Polychromophilus and Hepatocystis taxa, including several novel host associations. Notably, Hepatocystis was detected in Emballonuridae for the first time and occurred across multiple bat families. We substantially expand sampling of a previously described Scotophilus-associated Polychromophilus lineage and demonstrate its remarkable genetic conservation across geographic regions. In contrast, Hepatocystis parasites exhibited substantial genetic diversity across multiple host taxa. Multi-gene analyses expanded phylogenetic representation of bat-associated Hepatocystis and revealed close relationships between some bat- and squirrel-associated lineages. These data further suggest considerable diversity among Asian Hepatocystis parasites and phylogenetic patterns consistent with diversification across Asian host groups. Ecological analyses indicated that the infection varied more among host species and sampling sites than with measured host traits or landscape attributes and revealed pronounced seasonal differences in infection probability together with lower infection rate in more densely populated l

papers.title: Characterization of the type I subgroup d IFN gene locus in large yellow croaker (larimichthys crocea) reveals a transposition-associated mechanism of type I IFN gene expansion in teleosts.
papers.abstract: Type I interferons (IFNs) are key innate immune cytokines and have undergone extensive lineage-specific gene expansion during vertebrate evolution. Although IFN gene expansion has traditionally been attributed to local tandem duplication, whether alternative genomic mechanisms contribute to the diversification of type I IFN genes remains largely unexplored. Here, we identified an unusual expansion pattern of the type I subgroup d IFN gene (IFNd) in the large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea, Lc), revealing a potential transposition-associated mechanism underlying the duplication and relocation of an intron-containing type I IFN genomic module. Comparative genomic analyses suggest that IFNd genes in all fish species examined are conserved at the immunoglobulin-associated beta (CD79b)-pleckstrin homology and RUN domain containing M1 protein (PLEKHM1) locus, whereas sciaenid species possess an additional head-to-head IFNd pair within the F-box and WD repeat-containing protein (FBXW10)-PR/SET domain 9 (PRDM9) intergenic region. Phylogenetic analyses indicate that these duplicated copies originated from the ancestral sciaenid IFNd clade. The additional IFNd locus retains the conserved IFNd genomic architecture, including gene organization, intron-exon structure, and flanking genomic elements, supporting the duplication and relocation of an intact IFNd-containing module. The presence of repetitive sequences near the inserted locus further suggests that genome rearrangement-associated processes may have contributed to the expansion event. Molecular dating suggests that the emergence of the additional IFNd module occurred after the divergence of sciaenids from other percomorph lineages but before diversification of extant sciaenid species. The present study thus provides evidence supporting the hypothesis that transposition-associated duplication and long-range relocation of intact IFN genomic modules represent an additional mechanism contributing to type I IFN gene expa

papers.title: Description of a new species of Therodamas (Crustacea: Ergasilidae) from the gills of Trachelyopterus galeatus (Auchenipteridae) from the Brazilian Amazon.
papers.journal: Revista brasileira de parasitologia veterinaria = Brazilian journal of veterinary parasitology : Orgao Oficial do Colegio Brasileiro de Parasitologia Veterinaria
papers.abstract: Therodamas comprises copepods that parasitize marine, brackish-water and freshwater fishes, and currently includes eight valid species. In this study, a new species for this genus was described from the gills of Trachelyopterus galeatus collected in the Jari River, eastern Amazon, Brazil. Parasites were analyzed using light microscopy, scanning electron microscopy and SSU-rDNA sequences. A total of 539 parasites has recovered, with prevalence of 69%, mean intensity of 18 parasites per host and mean abundance of 12 (standard deviation = 12.8). The new species, Therodamas anujauensis n. sp., is characterized by the absence of cephalic lobes, an elongated neck and a distinctive combination of setae and spines on the swimming legs. Phylogenetic analyses confirmed its placement within Ergasilidae and revealed a close relationship with Therodamas longicollum. Molecular dating suggested that the Therodamas lineage originated approximately 59.6 million years ago, whereas the divergence between T. anujauensis n. sp. and T. longicollum occurred about 6.03 million years ago. This study increases the number of known species of Therodamas from eight to nine and expands knowledge of parasite diversity in the Amazon region.

papers.title: Deep-sea siliceous sponges harbor distinct and functionally diverse microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Sponges, phylum Porifera, are long-lived and basal-branching metazoans that play important roles in ocean biogeochemistry and host diverse microbial communities. Siliceous sponges form a major clade of the Porifera; however, their microbiome is not well characterized, particularly in the deep ocean. Here, we used shotgun metagenomics to investigate the composition of the microbial communities of 13 siliceous sponges collected from four sites near Puerto Rico from depths ranging from 400 to 1,900 meters. Nine of the sponges in this study are from five sponge families that have not previously been sequenced using shotgun metagenomics. We assembled a total of 176 metagenome-assembled genomes from 20 bacterial phyla and 1 archaeal phylum. Ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA) Nitrosopumilaceae dominated most siliceous sponge microbial communities and was strikingly the sole symbiont associated with one sponge (Farrea). Overall, microbiome diversity was relatively low across siliceous sponges, except for a Phloeodictyidae, which is likely a high microbial abundance (HMA) sponge. Our results suggest that host sponge phylogeny may shape microbial community structure, with limited evidence for an environmental role. The sponge-associated microbial communities contained genetic capabilities for diverse metabolic functions, particularly contributing to the carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur cycles. In addition to the AOA, evidence of potential for microbial autotrophy was found through the presence of genes for RuBisCO, methanotrophy, and ATP citrate lyase. papers.title: Somatization in patients with borderline personality disorder compared to healthy controls: The mediating roles of self- and other-mentalizing in the effect of attachment insecurity.
papers.abstract: AIM: Somatization is frequently observed in patients with borderline personality disorder (BPD). BPD is characterized by difficulties in mentalizing capacity. This study aimed to examine somatization in BPD patients compared with a healthy control group, focusing on the roles of self- and other-mentalizing in the relationship between attachment insecurity and somatic symptoms. METHOD: A total of 164 individuals, including 82 patients diagnosed with BPD and 82 healthy controls, participated in our study between August 2023 and March 2024. Somatization Scale, Experiences in Close Relationships-Revised, Trait Meta-Mood Scale, Mentalization Scale, Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test were used to assess somatization, dimensions of attachment insecurity, self- and other-mentalizing. Moderated mediation analysis was conducted using Model 15 in the PROCESS macro added to SPSS. RESULTS: Somatization was observed to be more pronounced in patients with BPD compared to healthy controls. Self- and other-mentalizing were closely related to somatization in BPD patients. It was demonstrated with moderated mediation analysis that clarity of feelings and mind-reading ability mediated the association between attachment anxiety and somatization in BPD patients. In healthy controls, only clarity of feelings partially mediated this association. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that self- and other-mentalizing may serve as protective factors against the increased somatization observed in patients with BPD. Deficiencies in these mentalizing abilities may be linked to somatization due to difficulties in interpreting bodily signals and dealing with emotional distress from unstable relationships.

papers.title: cis-Carboxylate Enhancement of Mn(III)-OH Hydrogen Atom Abstraction through PCET Thermodynamics.
papers.abstract: Manganese(III)-hydroxo intermediates are proposed as key hydrogen atom abstraction (HAA) species in manganese-dependent enzymes, yet how first-sphere carboxylate ligands control their proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) thermodynamics remains poorly understood. Here, a cis-(carboxylato)(hydroxo) manganese(III) complex, [MnIII(TBDAP)(OH)(C6H5COO)]+ (1), is investigated as a functional model of the manganese lipoxygenase active site. Comparison with an alkoxide analogue, [MnIII(TBDAP)(OH)(C6H5CH2O)]+ (2), reveals a 3000-fold enhancement in HAA reactivity and a large kinetic isotope effect consistent with tunneling-assisted hydrogen transfer. Redox titration experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support a cooperative thermodynamic contribution involving a positive shift in MnIII/II redox potential and a computationally predicted increase in hydroxo pKa associated with intramolecular hydrogen bonding, leading to an increased O-H bond dissociation free energy. Para-substituted benzoate derivatives show only modest changes in HAA rates despite electronic perturbations, consistent with possible partial thermodynamic compensation. The results highlight the role of first-sphere ligand environments in regulating metal-hydroxo reactivity through PCET thermodynamics and provide design principles for biological and synthetic oxidation chemistry. A structurally defined cis-carboxylate dramatically enhances the hydrogen atom abstraction reactivity of a Mn(III)-OH complex. A 3000-fold rate acceleration, combined with redox measurements and DFT calculations, reveals cooperative control of PCET thermodynamics and provides insight into how first-sphere carboxylate ligands tune biologically relevant metal-hydroxo intermediates.

papers.title: Communication surrounding cesarean delivery: A secondary analysis on a qualitative study evaluating women's experiences of perceived preparedness, agency, and psychological well-being.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cesarean delivery is associated with an elevated risk of perinatal mood, anxiety, and trauma symptoms. Though anesthetic and surgical techniques are well studied, less attention has been given to how perioperative communication, including consultation with an anesthesiology provider, shapes patient experience and psychological outcomes. METHODS: We conducted a secondary qualitative analysis of focus group transcripts originally collected during the development of an intervention to prevent postpartum mental health challenges following cesarean delivery. Twenty-two participants with lived experience of cesarean delivery discussed communication with their obstetric, anesthesia, and perioperative care teams. Transcripts were reanalyzed using a qualitative approach focused on communication-related themes. RESULTS: Three domains emerged: communication gaps, communication content, and communication impact. Participants described limited preparation for the possibility of cesarean delivery, insufficient information about intraoperative sensations and recovery, lack of partner inclusion, and few opportunities for postoperative debriefing. Anticipatory guidance that helped patients form a mental map of the procedure and real-time explanations using shared decision-making with the anesthesiology team were some of the most valued communication experiences and were described as fostering agency. Communication gaps were perceived by participants as shaping their psychological well-being, trust in the medical teams, sense of control, physical recovery, and early parent-infant bonding. CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative communication perceived by participants to be a central, modifiable factor shaping psychological experience surrounding the delivery. Trauma-informed, anticipatory, and real-time communication, involving all medical service lines, represents a critical opportunity to improve patient-centered care and may help mitigate perinatal mood and anxiety disorders.

papers.title: Nonlinear Quantum Effects Drive Grotthuss Proton Conduction in Structured Electrolytes Based on Deep Eutectic Solvents.
papers.abstract: Structured electrolytes based on deep eutectic solvents (DESs) face electrochemical limitations of vehicular diffusion due to high viscosities often leading to low conductivities. Here, we demonstrate that the inverse relationship between viscosity and conductivity in DESs can be circumvented by leveraging their hydrogen bonding networks for Grotthuss proton transport. Using DESs comprising imidazole and levulinic acid, we show that the existence of extended hydrogen-bonded chains coupled with rapid reorientation of protonated imidazoles result in enhanced Grotthuss proton diffusion in these concentrated hydrogen-bonded electrolyte systems. Key machine-learning driven simulations - crucially incorporating nuclear quantum effects (NQEs) - validate our experimental findings, which classical simulations fail to capture. This study demonstrates that NQEs promote imidazole protonation, catalyze the hydrogen-bonded chain formation, and influence chain reorientation, resulting in enhanced dynamics surpassing classical predictions in structured electrolytes. While the conclusions are drawn here for a particular imidazole/acid system, they are expected to apply broadly to protic DESs that support chain-like structures and exploit Grotthuss diffusion as the primary charge-transport mechanism.

papers.title: Hydroxy-Functionalized Near-Infrared Squaraine Dyes for Advanced Organic Conjugates and Hybrid Materials.
papers.abstract: Near-infrared squaraine dyes absorbing beyond 900 nm are promising for use in sensing and imaging, as photothermal additives or as complementary materials for energy conversion applications. Here, the synthesis of alkyl hydroxy-functionalized, benz[cd]indole-donor capped squaraine dyes using the squaric acid and the dicyanomethylene-substituted squaraine acceptor unit is reported. In parallel synthesis, the hydroxy group is introduced either directly on the dye-solubilizing alkyl side chains or coupled to the aryl part of the donor, and one or two functional linkers are attached. The hydroxy-functionalized dyes are then esterified with carboxyl groups attached to silica nanoparticles, a meltable polymer and a fullerene electron acceptor. Properties of the resulting hybrid material and organic conjugates demonstrate application merits of covalent bonding over blending for targeted photoinduced emission, heat and charge transfer reactions using near-infrared squaraine dyes.

papers.title: Polymer-mediated mineralization in hydrogels: design principles, hybrid materials, and network visualization.
papers.abstract: Polymer-mediated mineralization in hydrogels offers a versatile route to inorganic-organic hybrids in which mineral formation is coupled to network chemical affinity, precursor transport, spatial confinement, and mechanics. This review first distills the biomineralization concepts most relevant to hydrogel design, including classical and nonclassical nucleation, precursor stabilization, and charge-regulated ion binding. We then organize hydrogel-mineral systems around four experimentally useful variables: chemical affinity, precursor transport, spatial confinement, and network reorganization kinetics. Their interplay governs where nucleation occurs, how amorphous precursors transform, and what architecture is produced. We subsequently distinguish these formation-stage processes from load-induced mechanical relaxation and dissipation in the resulting hybrid materials, which contribute to reinforcement, damage tolerance, interfacial bonding, or time-programmed functions. We further discuss mineralization-assisted electron microscopy, which converts selected polymer networks into electron-dense replicas for direct visualization of mesh structure, heterogeneity, defects, and surface chains, together with emerging image-processing routes for quantitative analysis. Finally, we outline opportunities in dynamic mineralization, hierarchical organization, structural digital twins, and data-driven materials design.

papers.title: A Fight for All Women: Social Change as a Framework for Meaning Among Professionals Working With Gender-Based Violence Survivors.
papers.abstract: Research on work with survivors of gender-based violence (GBV) has primarily focused on its emotional burden and implications for practitioners' well-being. This study explores how professionals working in GBV services experience and make sense of their work, drawing on 23 interviews analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Participants' accounts revealed challenges related to the persistence of GBV and sexism in society and to job precarity, but also highlighted the meaning they attribute to their work as a political commitment to supporting women and contributing to social change. The findings underscore the importance of understanding practitioners' well-being within the broader social and political context of GBV work.

papers.title: Lactate Signal: Modulator of Cellular Energy Production and Anabolism.
papers.abstract: Lactate is no longer viewed simply as a glycolytic end-product, but as a compartmentalized signaling metabolite that coordinates energy production, carbon redistribution, redox balance, and anabolic commitment. This review discusses lactate as a regulator of the catabolism-anabolism axis, emphasizing two major patterns of molecular interpretation. First, lactate acts through non-covalent mechanisms, including transporter-mediated flux, receptor-dependent sensing, pH-linked effects, and direct binding to intracellular proteins. These processes allow lactate-rich states to rapidly couple metabolic flux to signaling pathways. Second, lactate-associated metabolic states are translated into the dynamic and reversible change of covalent post-translational modifications, including histone and non-histone lactylation. Histone lactylation connects glycolytic metabolism to transcriptional regulation, whereas non-histone lactylation expands lactate-dependent control to immune signaling, mitochondrial metabolism, DNA repair, cardiovascular stress, tissue remodeling, and cancer progression. We further discuss how extracellular, cytosolic, mitochondrial-associated, and nuclear lactate pools provide distinct biochemical contexts in which lactate-dependent mechanisms can operate. By integrating lactate transport, receptor sensing, protein binding, metabolism, and lactylation, this Review uses compartmental organization as a framework for synthesizing how lactate-rich states influence metabolic adaptation, stress responses, immune regulation, tissue remodeling, disease progression, and, in selected contexts, anabolic or reparative programs.

papers.title: The Shadows of Internalized Bisexual Myths: Jealousy and Psychological Intimate Partner Violence Perpetration Among Bisexual + Individuals in Turkiye.
papers.abstract: Bisexual+ (bi+) individuals may face unique challenges stemming from the internalization of myths related to their sexual orientation. This internalization may make individuals more sensitive to perceived threats in their relationships, which can increase feelings of jealousy. In turn, internalized bisexual myths and heightened jealousy may contribute to the perpetration of psychological intimate partner violence (IPV) within bi+ relationships. Thus, in this study, we aimed to examine the parallel mediating roles of cognitive and emotional jealousy in the association between internalized bisexual myths and psychological IPV perpetration. A sample of 230 bi+ individuals from Türkiye completed the (Internalized) Bisexual Myths Scale, the Multidimensional Jealousy Scale, and the Multidimensional Measure of Emotional Abuse Short Form. Overall, 94.3% of bi+ individuals reported perpetrating at least one act of psychological IPV against their partners within the past 6 months. Results from the parallel mediation analyses revealed that both cognitive and emotional jealousy mediated the relationship between internalized bisexual myths and psychological IPV perpetration. These findings suggest that bi+ individuals who internalize bisexual myths and exhibit higher levels of emotional and cognitive jealousy may be more susceptible to perpetrating psychological IPV against their partners. This study underscores the need for further research to better understand psychological IPV perpetration among bi+ individuals, highlighting the value of qualitative and longitudinal methods for gaining deeper insights.

papers.title: Exploring the Pathways of Childhood Adversity on Intimate Partner Violence Among Men Who Have Sex with Men: A Network Analysis.
papers.abstract: The high prevalence of intimate partner violence (IPV), childhood adversity, and psychological factors has been observed among men who have sex with men (MSM) in China. Nevertheless, the intrinsic correlation between the three remains to be fully understood. Consequently, there is an urgent need for research that explores their interrelationships. This study aimed to reveal the long-term mechanisms and potential pathways of childhood adversity on the development of IPV in the Chinese MSM population, to mitigate the long-term effects of childhood adversity, and ultimately reduce the incidence of IPV. This study used a cross-sectional survey to recruit 1,130 MSM participants in three Chinese cities. In this population, we utilized network analysis and path analysis to further explore the relationship between childhood adversity, psychological factors, and IPV. The results of the network analysis suggested that psychological factors may play an important mediating role between childhood adversity and IPV. The results of the path analysis indicated that adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) (β = .08, p = .013) and parental rejection (β = .10, p = .03) were direct risk factors for IPV. In addition, childhood adversity played an indirect role in IPV through psychological factors. In conclusion, the prevalence of childhood adversity, mental health problems, and IPV is high in the Chinese MSM population. The presence of ACEs and parental rejection predisposes individuals to IPV through the mediation of psychological factors. Our findings suggested that proximal prevention is imperative for the mitigation of the long-term effects of childhood adversity to reduce the incidence of IPV in the Chinese MSM population.

papers.title: Facial Asymmetry and Sexuality in Women.
papers.abstract: People perceive more symmetrical individuals as more attractive; therefore, facial symmetry has been linked to mate selection. Being perceived as more attractive could also increase women's indirect reproductive benefits that would follow from pronounced sexuality and enhanced mating. Sexuality can be examined either as long-term, through sociosexual orientation, or through current sexual activity and desire. This study explored the relationship between facial asymmetry and female sexuality, while taking into account a relationship status and, due to the potential differences in facial asymmetry between female from rural and urban areas, the place of residence. Long-term sexuality was measured with the three subscales of the Sociosexual Orientation Inventory (SOI-R): Behavior, Attitude, and Desire. Current sexual activity and desire were assessed with questions about their frequency and intensity (based on the Female Sexual Function Index). Simple correlations revealed a weak, negative association between facial asymmetry and the number of sexual partners in the last year (ρ = - .23, 95% CI [- 0.45, 0.01], p = .047), SOI Attitude (ρ = - .25, 95% CI [- 0.44, - 0.03], p = .031), and sexual desire (ρ = - .21, 95% CI [- 0.43, - 0,00], p = .082). However, these effects were no longer significant after including place of residence as a confounder (.42 < p < .91). These results highlight the importance of external conditions when investigating correlates of facial asymmetry.

papers.title: Toward a Field That Prevents Harm Before It Begins: A Reflection and Research Agenda for Interpersonal Violence Prevention.
papers.abstract: Interpersonal violence research has established the profound developmental, relational, and societal consequences of violence; the next challenge is preventing harm before it occurs. This commentary honors Jon Conte's contributions to the field by advancing a 5-year research and practice agenda that positions corporal punishment and No Hit Zones within a broader, integrated framework for interpersonal violence prevention. Drawing on ecological, public health, social norms, and implementation science perspectives, it identifies priorities for investigating mechanisms of norm change, bystander intervention, institutional trust and equity, implementation at scale, longitudinal behavioral outcomes, and cross-violence pathways across the lifespan. The proposed agenda emphasizes creating universal nonviolence environments while pairing clear behavioral norms with practical family supports, community-engaged communication, and supportive policy. Progress requires connecting child maltreatment prevention with efforts addressing intimate partner violence, sexual violence, bullying, and community violence to build environments in which nonviolence is expected, supported, equitable, and sustainable.

papers.title: Victim characteristics of stalking in a nationally representative sample, USA.
papers.journal: Injury prevention : journal of the International Society for Child and Adolescent Injury Prevention
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Stalking is a serious public health problem experienced by millions of women and men. The National Intimate Partner and Sexual Violence Survey is a nationally representative survey that collects victimisation data on sexual violence, stalking and intimate partner violence in the USA. This article presents 2023/2024 national prevalence estimates by race/ethnicity and age at first stalking victimisation among victims. METHODS: We analysed data from 15 609 participants who completed the 2023/2024 National Intimate Partner and Sexual Violence Survey. Lifetime prevalence estimates and significance testing were calculated for stalking by race/ethnicity and age at first-time stalking victimisation and weighted to the US adult population. RESULTS: Stalking prevalence varied by race/ethnicity. For example, 29.8% and 13.9% of non-Hispanic multiracial/other women and men, 22.0% and 12.8% of Hispanic women and men and 23.0% and 8.3% of non-Hispanic White women and men, respectively, were stalked during their lifetimes. Stalking was more prevalent for women and significant differences were observed across racial/ethnic groups. Most female and male stalking victims first experienced stalking before age 25, with approximately 30% experiencing it before turning 18. Differences between women and men within each age-at-first victimization group were not significant. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS: Stalking is a serious problem impacting individuals across all racial/ethnic groups and often begins in younger years. To tailor prevention efforts, future studies may examine how victim-perpetrator relationships and stalking tactics vary by race/ethnicity and age of victims. Stalking is preventable and requires ongoing monitoring to shape prevention strategies and reduce its negative impacts.

papers.title: It Ends With Us… But Not for Intimate Partner Violence Victims.
papers.abstract: The movie It Ends With Us reached millions of viewers. It is important to determine whether popular media changes IPV-accepting attitudes, like minimization and victim blaming. IPV victims who saw the movie reported less acceptance of coercive control and more abuse acceptance than victims who had not seen it. There were no differences among nonvictims. This suggests the movie was a flawed vehicle for IPV attitude change. Popular media represents an important mechanism of change for IPV-related social norms but requires rigorous assessment of effectiveness. Diversity concerns and potential negative impacts are of particular concern.

papers.title: Through an anxious lens: The roles of adolescents' anxiety symptoms in conditioning the relational consequences of parental responses to negative emotions through shaping adolescents' appraisals of parental responses.
papers.journal: Journal of research on adolescence : the official journal of the Society for Research on Adolescence
papers.abstract: Grounded in the cognitive-affective models of anxiety and the emotion socialization theory, the present study aimed to examine how adolescents' anxiety symptoms may moderate the associations of parental earlier responses to adolescents' negative emotions with the subsequent adolescent-parent relationship quality, and whether the moderating roles of adolescents' anxiety would be mediated by adolescents' appraisals of parental responses. Two-wave longitudinal data were obtained from 335 Chinese adolescent-parent dyads (41.8% boys, Mage = 16.08 years; 72.2% mothers, Mage = 42.05 years). Results of mediated moderation model analyses indicated that adolescent anxiety symptoms (Time 1) negatively predicted adolescents' positive appraisals of supportive responses and didactic talk responses to adolescents' negative emotions (Time 2). Nevertheless, adolescent anxiety symptoms (Time 1) only moderated the association between parental didactic talk and teaching (Time 1) and parent-adolescent relationship quality (Time 2), such that didactic talk and teaching predicted better subsequent relationship quality only among adolescents with low levels of anxiety symptoms. This moderation effect was partially explained by adolescents' appraisals of didactic talk and teaching, as adolescents with lower levels of anxiety symptoms tended to interpret this response more benignly, which, in turn, predicted better subsequent parent-adolescent relationship quality. In conclusion, the relational implications of parental didactic talk and teaching may depend partly on adolescents' anxiety symptoms and their appraisals of such parental responses, highlighting the importance of considering adolescents' individual characteristics and subjective interpretations in parental emotion socialization.
